The runner takes that one match and does not reject ambiguity; an index past the last match never attaches (assertion_timeout). Use it only when the target is genuinely the nth item of a list, never to paper over an ambiguous locator. Count predicates refuse a locator with nth.

resourceRef.description: Id of the request step that creates the resource and declares input.resource with handle and ownerProof; with find, the id of the plan step that creates the data

resource.description: Declares the resource this request creates so a cleanup entry can delete it. Needs both handle and ownerProof, and a top-level cleanup entry whose resourceRef is this step's id; otherwise the cleanup never runs (cleanup_never_runs)

handle.description: JSON pointer to the new resource's id in this request's response

ownerProof.description: JSON pointer to a response field proving the run's account owns the resource (creator, user or tenant id)

input.description: The deletion request, run once the resource is known (with find, once exactly one item matched)

find.description: Cleanup by lookup. resourceRef then names the plan step that creates the data through the UI (any step, not a request step with input.resource). Run before the cleanup of request-created resources, in reverse order of the entries. No match: nothing is deleted and the cleanup passes; two or more matches, or a match without handle or ownerProof: nothing is deleted and the cleanup fails or is inconclusive; never the first match

resourceType.description: Kind of the data the lookup finds (for example project); recorded on the resource and shown to the approver of a manual cleanup

resource.description: Declares the resource this request creates so a cleanup entry can delete it. Needs both handle and ownerProof, and a top-level cleanup entry whose resourceRef is this step's id; otherwise the cleanup never runs (cleanup_never_runs)

handle.description: JSON pointer to the new resource's id in this request's response

ownerProof.description: JSON pointer to a response field proving the run's account owns the resource (creator, user or tenant id)

lookup.description: GET request run at cleanup time that lists the items (a list or search route of the application). It takes no body, capture or resource, and no variableRef that only the cleanup defines

itemsPointer.description: JSON pointer to the array of items in the lookup response; "" when the response body is the array

keyPointer.description: JSON pointer inside each item to the field compared with equals (for example /name)

equals.description: The value the plan gave the data when a step created it. Scalar and never sensitive (no secretRef, no sensitive capture): it is stored as the resource's correlation key. Pick a value no other data of the account has, for example one carrying a captured or dependency value unique to the run

handlePointer.description: JSON pointer inside the matched item to the id the deletion request uses; the input refers to it as {"variableRef": "<resourceRef>.handle"}

ownerProofPointer.description: JSON pointer inside the matched item to a field proving the run's account owns it (creator, user or tenant id). A match without it is never deleted

totalPointer.description: JSON pointer to the total item count in the lookup response. When the total exceeds the items returned, or the response has a Link header with rel=next, the list is paged and the cleanup ends inconclusive instead of reading zero matches as nothing created

successPredicate.description: Cleanup runs after the steps, also when a step already deleted the resource: accept the deletion route's answer for a missing resource too (for example statusIn [200, 404])
